Package hadur117.core.move

Class MoveController

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.move.MoveController
public class MoveController extends Object
What the duel's surf knows about the enemy's gun: its waves in flight, the KNN danger views that score where on a wave its bullets go, its hit rate on us, and our bullets in flight with the shadows they cast on its waves (MOVE-1). SurfMover decides where to drive; this class answers how dangerous a place on a wave is.

Where it sits in the tick. HadurCore drives it only in the duel posture. Each scan adds an enemy wave at the power the enemy last fired (addWave(hadur117.core.model.Wave), guessBulletPower()); when the energy ledger explains a drop as a shot (WAVE-1, WAVE-2), updateFiringWave(long, long, double, boolean) marks the matching wave as a real bullet, and only firing waves are surfed, scored or counted. Each duel tick then runs setKShare(double) (TIME-1, TIME-2), checkWaves(long, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double) (break waves that have passed us and learn from them), takeBrokenWaveOutcomes() (read by the distance and flavour policies), updateShadows(long) (MOVE-1) and finally SurfMover.move(hadur117.core.model.BotOrders.Builder, hadur117.core.model.RobotState, hadur117.core.move.MoveController, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, int, boolean), which asks findSurfableWave(int, hadur117.core.model.RobotState) and getDangerScore(hadur117.core.model.Wave, hadur117.core.model.Wave.Intersection, int). Bullet events arrive through logBulletHit(hadur117.core.model.Wave, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, int, long), ourBulletFired(hadur117.core.move.OurBullet) and ourBulletGone(double, double).

Danger views. Eleven KnnViews hold past guess factors, each in its own feature space (SimpleFormula, MoveFormula, FlattenerFormula). Most learn only from bullets that hit us; the flatteners learn from every wave that breaks. Each view is on only while the enemy's normalised hit rate on us clears its thresholds, so a gun that rarely hits meets only the simple view, and one that hits often meets the recent and flattener views too. The hit rate is normalised: each hit counts 0.1 / (our angular width), scaled by the wave's escape-angle range, so hits from close range (where we look wide) count for less than hits from afar.

Opponent memory. The opening book can hand in the profile's hit rate as a prior (setPrior(double, double)), which decides the views while it is more certain than the live estimate (DIAL-1, ADAPT-2); it can force the flatteners on (setFlattenerFirst(boolean), ADAPT-2, and MOVE-2's first flavour); and it replays stored hits as seeds that weigh their SeedWeight against a live sample's 1 (seed(double[], hadur117.core.model.SeedWeight), ADAPT-3). RES-4 takes the prior away (clearPrior()) and fades the seeds' weight.

Units and conventions. Angles are radians on Robocode's compass (0 north, clockwise); guess factors are the firing angle's offset from the wave's bearing to us, signed by our orbit direction, over the wave's maximum escape angle (nominally in [-1, 1]); hit percentages and their margins are in percent, hit rates are fractions.

Bounds (RES-2). Each view caps its points (KnnView.DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_POINTS or its own limit); waves are dropped by the WaveManager when they break and at each round; our bullets leave the list when an event names them, when they leave the field, or at the round's start; the broken-wave outcomes are drained each tick.

The move package never sees the gun, melee, memory, adapt, policy or posture packages (the ArchUnit rules): every decision from them comes in through the setters here.

    • ourBulletGone

      public void ourBulletGone(double heading, double power)
      MOVE-1: one of our bullets hit, missed or met a bullet. The engine names it by heading and power; an event without a heading (NaN) stands for the oldest bullet of that power. An event that matches no bullet (one already dropped off the field, say) changes nothing.
      Parameters:

    • getDangerScore

      public double getDangerScore(Wave w, Wave.Intersection intersection, int surfWaveIndex)
      How dangerous it is to be at intersection when wave w breaks, by the views that are on: a weighted average, in [0, 1], of how close each neighbour's firing angle falls to the intersection. The shadow (MOVE-1), the bullet's damage and its time to impact are applied by SurfMover, not here.

      Each neighbour found for the wave (the enemy's past firing situations most like this one) contributes a kernel 2^-|u|, where u is the distance from its firing angle to the intersection's centre in units of the intersection's half-width: 1 at the centre, 1/2 at our edge, and falling off beyond. A neighbour weighs its age decay, over its feature-space distance, times its seed weight (ADAPT-3). Each view's weighted sum is multiplied by the view's weight; the total is divided by the total weight, so the result is an average, not a sum.

      When no view is on with data, or all neighbours weigh nothing (faded seeds, RES-4), it falls back to a fixed guess: a head-on gun and one aiming near the escape angle.

      Parameters:
      w - the wave being surfed
      intersection - the firing angles that would hit us (centre and half-width)
      surfWaveIndex - the wave's index among the surfable waves, which keys the neighbour cache
      Returns:
      the danger, in [0, 1] from the views; the fallback's sum can be up to 4

    • getDangerScore

      double getDangerScore(Wave w, Wave.Intersection intersection, int surfWaveIndex, double[] parts)
      AES-1: getDangerScore(hadur117.core.model.Wave, hadur117.core.model.Wave.Intersection, int), also writing each view's two sums into parts when it is not null: parts[i] is view i's weight times its density, parts[n + i] its weight times its scan weight (both 0 for a view that is off or empty), and parts[2n] the fallback's danger when the fallback was used, else NaN. The score is the sum of the first n over the sum of the next n. Measurement only.
      Parameters:
      parts - null, or at least 2 * viewCount() + 1 long

The views are the ones getDangerScore(hadur117.core.model.Wave, hadur117.core.model.Wave.Intersection, int) averages, with the same kernel and shadows: view i's danger is its density over its scan weight, and its share is its weight times its scan weight, normalised to sum to 1, so the weighted mean of the dangers is getDangerScore(hadur117.core.model.Wave, hadur117.core.model.Wave.Intersection, int) (less its no-data fallback).
